Here is why, one level down: two threads each increment a shared counter a million times...'. In ch16-races-p3: 'The classic fix is the mutex of Chapter 4, a lock only one thread can hold...'
reason: Ch4 (ipc-p12) and Ch7 (gil-p2) both already show the lost update, and Ch4 already introduces the mutex as a semaphore of one. Ch16 presents the example as new and never refers back. The instruction-level cause is new, so the example stays and only back-references are needed.
judge_fix: ch16-races-p1, after the first sentence: 'Chapter 4 lost an addition between two processes and Chapter 7 a reference count between two threads; here is the cause, one level down.' Then keep 'The classic example sounds harmless: ...'. ch16-races-p3: 'The classic fix is a mutex (mutual exclusion lock, the one-at-a-time semaphore of Chapter 4).'
